claim: In a concentrated (20-stock) monthly-rebalanced US momentum portfolio, 1991-2024, the CAGR gap between the best and worst trading day of the month was 348 bp; splitting into 2-20 tranches left the mean CAGR (16.7-16.8%) and Sharpe (0.59-0.60) unchanged while shrinking the dispersion from 3.48% to 0-2%. Single-day max drawdowns ranged -69.3% to -74.9%.
limitations: Snapshot is pdftotext of the fetched PDF (PDF kept beside it). Stock-level momentum, no costs in the RTL table, not leveraged ETFs, no drawdown figures for the tranched books.
independent_replication: Hoffstein, Faber, Braun (SSRN 3673910) report >100 bp annualized RTL for momentum and other factor indices.

claim: Factor indices (value, size, momentum, quality, low vol) show rebalance timing luck often above 100 bp annualized, larger for concentrated and less frequently rebalanced portfolios.
limitations: Abstract page read; SSRN PDF blocked to the fetcher. Stock factor indices, not leveraged ETF rotation.
independent_replication: Concretum 2025 (348 bp on a momentum book).

claim: On a timing-luck-sensitive TAA strategy (Bold Asset Allocation), tranched portfolios averaged 14.2% a year against 13.9% for single-day ones, and the spread of possible annual returns fell by almost two thirds.
limitations: No drawdown numbers; different strategy family (TAA).
independent_replication: Concretum 2025 table 3 shows the same flat-mean result.
